BACKGROUND AND SUMMARY
This application is a request for approval of a Site Plant Amendment and Conditional Use
Permit for approximately 1.32 acres located on the south side of Pioneer Road, at
approximately 874 E. Pioneer Road (Exhibit B & C). The property is currently zoned TC. The
applicant is requesting that a Site Plan Amendment be approved to allow for the
development of the site with a new office building. As part of the Amended Site Plan the
applicant is also requesting approval of a Conditional Use Permit to install fencing in excess
of six feet (6’), up to a height of ten feet (10’), around a proposed basketball and sports
court.




Scalar New Office Building                                        App. #SPR-51-2022 & USE-52-2022
Site Plan Amendment and Conditional Use Permit Request   1
The existing building was originally constructed as the offices of the South Valley Sewer
District in 1986, before being sold to Green Shoot Holdings in 2016. The property consists
of Lot 1 of the South Valley Sewer District Subdivision recorded August 11, 2015 (Exhibit L).
A second parcel, a narrow inadvertent remainder parcel that was created when the South
Valley Sewer District subdivision was recorded, located just south of the southern property
line of lot 1 is also under the same ownership, but is not a part of this application. This
narrow parcel equals 0.02 acres in size.

A previous Site Plan Amendment for the property proposing to renovate and expand the
existing building on site was approved by the Planning Commission on July 22, 2021.
Construction per those plans was not begun and this new proposal will replace the prior
development plan.

According to Draper City Municipal Code (DCMC) Section 9-8-020 the purpose of the TC
zone is to “provide a method for implementing special provisions found within the general plan
and the Draper City conservation area master plan regarding the establishment and promotion
of a historic core area of the community characterized by stringent design standards for
buildings, public spaces, site design and landscaping with a harmonious mix of commercial uses,
limited high density residential uses and civic areas.”

Site Plan Layout. The proposal includes removal of the existing building and construction of
a new two story office building (Exhibit F). The lot is a corner lot and the new proposed
building would be setback from the front property lines 10.7 feet on the north and
between 14.3 feet on the east. The setbacks conform to the requirements of the TC zone.
The ground floor will cover an area of approximately 10,335 ft2 and the total building
square footage of both floors will be approximately 20,598 ft2. A rooftop terrace will occupy
an area of approximately 3,660 ft2 located on the southern portion of the roof. The parking
lot is proposed to contain 72 parking spaces and will be located predominantly to the west
of the building. An employee amenity area and basketball and sports court will be located
in the southwest corner of the property. The applicant is requesting approval of

Landscaping and Lot Coverage. The landscaping plan (Exhibit G) complies with the
requirements of the TC zone and has approximately ten percent (10%) landscaping within
the parking area as required by the TC zone and twenty-five percent (25%) overall
landscape coverage of the site which exceeds the minimum required amount in the TC
zone by ten percent (10%). Outdoor amenities are required and the proposed site plan
(Exhibit F) provides for a rooftop terrace, 2nd floor rear balcony seating area, electrical
vehicle charging stations, basketball and sports court, ground level patio seating area, and
bike racks. There are four (4) Healthy mature trees that will be removed as part of the
planned construction of the building and parking expansions. These trees will be replaced
on the site by thirty-eight (38) additional trees in compliance with the requirements of the
TC zone. A majority of these replacement trees will be Taylor Junipers placed near the
baseline of the basketball and sports court to provide additional screening between the
court and the adjacent residential property.

Parking. According to the Site Plan (Exhibit F) the parking lot will contain 72 parking spaces.
Six (6) of these spaces, approximately eight percent (8%) of the total parking spaces, will be
marked as compact. The required parking for a general office building is four (4) spaces per
one-thousand square feet (1,000 ft2) of gross floor area. The reported gross building floor
area including the proposed expansion is 20,598 ft2 which would require a parking stall
count between 74 and 90 parking stalls per the natural adjustment range permitted in
ordinance. The applicant is requesting two deviations in regards to the parking, the first is
for a parking reduction to 72 stalls which is two (2) stalls less than the reductions allowed
under the natural adjustment range. A parking study has been submitted as part of this
requested deviation is attached in Exhibit J, and staff concurs with the methodology and
findings found in that report that the 72 stalls provided are sufficient to meet the average
parking demand for the building. The second deviation being requested is for the use of
tree diamonds rather than installing parking row dividing landscaping between rows of
adjacent parking.

Parking Modification. Chapter 25 of the DCMC makes provisions for the Planning
Commission to authorize a deviation to the strict compliance with the terms of the Code
regarding the calculation of the minimum number of required parking spaces and for the
use of tree diamonds.



Scalar New Office Building                                             App. #SPR-51-2022 & USE-52-2022
Site Plan Amendment and Conditional Use Permit Request   6
DCMC Section 9-25-090 states that the number of parking spaces may be modified to
provide flexibility beyond the 10% +/- allowed in DCMC in order to adapt to specific
circumstances, reduce potential environmental impacts, and conserve resources. The
deviation to strict compliance is justified based upon a parking study submitted by the
applicant (Exhibit J). In order to approve a deviation to strict compliance with the parking
requirements of the DCMC, the Planning Commission must make findings based on the
type of use under application. For the subject application, DCMC Subsection 9-25-
090(C)(4)(a) states:

        a. For commercial, retail, office, and mixed use developments, the planning commission
           must find that:
              (1) Adequate parking will be provided;
              (2) The total number of spaces that would otherwise be required for each individual
                 establishment in the development is overly burdensome for the site specific
                 factors of the application;
              (3) Estimated trade offs between businesses which are open when others are closed
                 will not overburden the parking provided;
              (4) There is an adequate availability of approved on street or shared parking for all
                 associated uses;
              (5) Site or use specific conditions or factors do not provide for compliance with the
                 parking calculation used or parking requirements outlined in section 9-25-100,
                 table 9-25-1 of this chapter;
              (6) Transportation alternatives, including proximity to transit stations, provide
                 adequate transportation to offset any reduction in parking; and
              (7) Any potential for future expansion or addition to the development will have or
                 will provide adequate parking for that expansion or addition;
              (8) ADA compliant parking requirements are not proposed for adjustment;

The applicant has also made a deviation request to the Planning Commission for the use of
tree diamonds (Exhibit L). For the subject application, DCMC Subsection 9-25-080(H)(2)
states:

    2. Parking Row Dividing Landscaping:
       a. Rows of adjacent parking shall be separated by landscaping of at least five feet (5') in
          width or nine feet (9') in width if vehicles are allowed to overhang the landscaping.
          Where the planning commission finds that it is not feasible for rows of parking to be
          separated by landscaping, parking areas shall be designed to include tree
          diamonds. In order to determine this feasibility, the planning commission must find
          that:
          (1) The site requires a deviation from strict compliance to reduce parking; or
          (2) The site would requires a deviation from strict compliance to reduce parking in
              order to implement such landscaping; and



Scalar New Office Building                                      App. #SPR-51-2022 & USE-52-2022
Site Plan Amendment and Conditional Use Permit Request   7
           (3) Constraints of the site would necessitate the elimination of required parking
               spaces or reduction of site boundary landscaping buffers in order to facilitate
               such landscaping.
        b. When tree diamonds are proposed, they shall be spaced no more than three (3)
           parking spaces apart and the area dedicated to the tree diamond shall be at least
           five by five feet (5 x 5') when square or at least five feet (5') in diameter when round or
           oval.

As the proposed Site Plan includes the deviation request to the parking count based upon
the submitted parking study found in Exhibit J, the application meets the first criterion
listed for consideration of the request to use tree diamonds. The third criterion is also
required to be met for parking diamonds to be approved. That criterion requires an
analysis regarding constraints of the site that would require the elimination of required
parking spaces or site boundary landscaping buffers in order to facilitate installation of the
parking row dividing landscaping. As no land use buffer is required between properties in
the same zone, the Planning Commission would need to find that it is not feasible to
separate rows of parking with landscaping at least a minimum of five-feet (5’) in width
without causing the elimination of required parking. The applicant’s letter outlining the
request (Exhibit L) cites the existence of public utility easements along the front property
lines as constraining potential relocation of the building to the north and to the east some
additional distance to accommodate the additional parking row dividing landscaping. Staff
also notes that the calculated average parking demand per the submitted parking study is
sixty-two (62) total parking stalls, which is ten (10) fewer stalls than are being proposed. As
the proposal as presented contains thirteen (13) pairs of head to head parking stalls in
adjacent rows, even if ten (10) of those pairs were simply eliminated by installing additional
landscaping opposite on one of the stalls in the pair, there would still be at least three (3)
pairs where head to head parking would still exist. While potential designs exist that would
provide parking at or above the average demand rate calculated in the parking study and
would not require the use of tree diamonds, they would also require further reduction to
the parking count below the seventy-two (72) spaces proposed and the seventy-four (74)
spaces required in ordinance. Staff is of the opinion that the third required criterion for
approval by the Planning Commission has also been met. The five (5) proposed tree
diamonds all measure five feet (5’) by five feet (5’) and comply with the minimum size
requirements of the ordinance.

Architectural Design Standards Modification. Chapter 22 of the DCMC allows the Planning
Commission to authorize deviations to strict compliance with the terms of DCMC regarding
development design standards. This application, being submitted prior to changes to
DCMC Section 9-22-030 that were recently enacted, is subject to the previous regulations.
Those regulations state that the Planning Commission may approve architectural plans
associated with development applications that deviate from the requirements of the DCMC
based on making certain required findings in whole. Per the regulations relevant to this
application, the Planning Commission must find that, the deviation is consistent with the
purpose and intent of the policies and development standards pertaining to the applicable
zoning district or land use category, that the deviation is in the benefit of the health, safety
and welfare of the city and the project, and that the application meets at least three of the
following conditions:

          1. The project contains amenities such as pedestrian and bike connectivity in
             excess of what is required in the development code and site plan review.
          2. The overall percentage of dedicated public or private landscape and open space
             area exceeds the required amount by more than ten percent (10%).
          3. The project is a transit oriented development (TOD) and provides connectivity to
             a transportation facility.
          4. Traffic impacts on the neighborhood are lessened through programs, such as
             creative design, traffic calming measures, companywide carpool or transit pass
             programs.
          5. The project is an accredited LEED development.
          6. The variations are consistent with the purpose of this chapter and any applicable
             master plan or ordinance.
          7. The project is required to create a consistent and compatible design in cases
             which involve redeveloped buildings, additions to existing buildings, minor
             structures added to a site, or new buildings within a previously approved phased
             project.




Scalar New Office Building                                    App. #SPR-51-2022 & USE-52-2022
Site Plan Amendment and Conditional Use Permit Request   11
          8. Additional landscape plant material is provided in an amount at least ten
             percent (10%) more than the minimum required, including additional planting
             beds, plants, trees or a combination thereof.
          9. The building design is a specific architectural style, such as contemporary or
             modern, which utilizes facade materials differently then prescribed in
             subsection 9-22-040F of this chapter and is designed by a licensed architect.
          10. The amount of primary materials used for a facade is at least ten percent (10%)
             greater than the minimum required amount.

The architect and applicants have submitted a deviation request letter per the regulations
in DCMC Section 9-22-030 at the time the initial application was submitted (Exhibit L). In the
letter from the architect they have provided their analysis of the minimum 3 criteria the
project is required to meet for consideration of a deviation from the building design
standards contained in DCMC Subsections 9-22-040(C)(2) and 9-22-040(D)(2) prior to
amendment. Staff concurs with the assertions made in the request letter that the site
complies with criteria numbers 1, 2, and 10 as listed above (note: the applicants letter
identifies criterion 10 above as criterion 9). The Planning Commission may determine if
criterion 6 is met in their opinion if necessary. The site has amenities in excess of ordinance
requirements, has an overall landscaped area 10% over the minimum required, and utilizes
brick on the south and west façades in an amount greater than ten percent 10%) over the
minimum.

Lighting. The applicant has submitted lighting plans including the required photometric
analyses as Exhibit I. These plans do not comply with ordinance requirements as currently
submitted. Staff recommends that the Planning Commission require as a condition of
approval that revised lighting plans that comply with ordinance be submitted to planning
staff for review and that the plans must meet the outdoor lighting criteria of ordinance and
be approved prior to approval of a land disturbance permit for the property.

Criteria For Approval. The criteria for review and potential approval of a Site Plan
Amendment request are found in Sections 9-5-090(E) of the DCMC. This section depicts the
standard of review for such requests as:

        E. Standards For Approval: The following standards shall apply to the approval of a site
            plan:
            1. The entire site shall be developed at one time unless a phased development plan is
               approved.
            2. A site plan shall conform to applicable standards set forth in this title, including but
               not limited to, building heights, setbacks, access points, parking, landscaping, and
               building materials.
            3. The proposed development plans meet the intent, goals, and objectives of the
               general plan and the purpose of the zone district in which the site is located.
            4. The public facilities and services in the area are adequate to support the subject
               development, as required by engineering standards and specifications.
            5. The proposed development plans comply with the engineering standards found in
               Titles 7, 8, 11, 12, 16, and 18 of this code, including traffic, storm water drainage,
               and utilities concerns.

The criteria for review and potential approval of a conditional use permit request is found
in Section 9-5-080(E) of the DCMC. This section depicts the standard of review for such
requests as:

        E. Approval Standards: The standards of this subsection shall apply to the issuance of a
            conditional use permit:
            1. A conditional use permit may be issued for a use to be located within a zone where
                 the particular conditional use is allowed by the use regulations of the zone.
            2. Reasonable conditions may be imposed as necessary to substantially mitigate
                 reasonably anticipated detrimental effects of the proposed use. These conditions
                 may include conditions concerning use, construction, character, location,
                 landscaping, screening, parking, hours of operation, and other matters relating to
                 the purposes and objectives of this section. Such conditions shall be expressly set
                 forth in the motion authorizing the conditional use permit.
            3. If the reasonably anticipated detrimental effects of a proposed conditional use
                 cannot be substantially mitigated by the imposition of reasonable conditions to
                 achieve compliance with applicable standards, the conditional use may be
                 denied.
            4. The following factors shall be reviewed and considered in determining whether a
                 conditional use permit application should be approved, approved with



Scalar New Office Building                                        App. #SPR-51-2022 & USE-52-2022
Site Plan Amendment and Conditional Use Permit Request   14
                 conditions, or denied because reasonable conditions cannot be imposed to
                 achieve compliance with applicable standards:
                 a. The harmony and compliance of the proposed use with the objectives and
                      requirements of the city's general plan and this title;
                 b. The suitability of the specific property for the proposed use;
                 c. Whether the proposed use or facility may be injurious to potential or existing
                      development in the vicinity;
                 d. The economic impact of the proposed facility or use on the surrounding area;
                 e. The aesthetic impact of the proposed facility or use on the surrounding area;
                 f. The safeguards proposed or provided to ensure adequate utilities,
                      transportation access, drainage, parking, loading space, lighting, screening,
                      landscaping, open space, fire protection, and pedestrian and vehicular
                      circulation;
                 g. The safeguards provided or proposed to prevent noxious or offensive emissions
                      such as noise, glare, dust, pollutants and odor from the proposed facility or
                      use; and
                 h. The impact of the proposed facility or use on the health, safety, and welfare of
                      the city, the area, and persons owning or leasing property in the area.
             5. The planning commission may request additional information as may be
                 reasonably needed to determine whether the requirements of this subsection E
                 can be met.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Planning Commission review the requests, receive public
comment, and make a decision based on the findings listed below and the criteria for
approval, or denial, as listed within the staff report.

If the Planning Commission decides to approve the requests, staff recommends they
include the following conditions of approval:

        1. That all requirements of the Draper City Engineering, Public Works, Building,
           Planning, and Fire Divisions are satisfied throughout the development of the site
           and the construction of all buildings on the site, including permitting.
        2. That all requirements of the geologic hazard and geotechnical report are
           satisfied throughout the development of the site and the construction of all
           buildings on the site.
        3. That the updated photometric and lighting plans be submitted for review and
           approval that that are in compliance with ordinance requirements and show
           accurate calculations, design and notations, and are stamped by the individual
           responsible for the drawings prior to issuance of a Land Disturbance Permit..
        4. That sewer and water provider availability letters must be provided at the time
           of the application for the Land Disturbance Permit.
        5. That a copy of the signed and recorded stormwater maintenance agreement
           must be provided prior to issuance of a Land Disturbance Permit.
        6. That the building and site be constructed in substantial compliance with the
           plans presented to the Planning Commission.

PARKING STUDY
March 30, 2022

Zak Nugent
Scalar - Chief Executive Officer

RE: Parking Demand Analysis for Scalar Office

Dear Zak,

In the completed condition the Scalar Corporate Office Building will feature 20,605sf and 72 parking spaces
as shown in Figure 1.




                                      Figure 1. Scalar Office Site Plan

City Requirements (City Code Table 9-25-1) are 4 stalls per 1,000sf of building floor space, which here
translates to 75 stalls, 3 stalls beyond what is being provided. In accordance with Section 9-25-090 of the
Draper City Code this parking demand analysis has been prepared at your request to pursue this variance.

The City requirement of 4 stalls per 1,000sf of building floor space is based on the average parking supply
(not demand) ratio of 4.0 spaces per 1,000sf associated with the study sites of Land Use Code 701 “Office
Building” in the 4th Edition of “Parking Generation” (PG) as published by the Institute of Transportation
Engineers (ITE). For more accurate demand estimating, the 5th and current edition of this publication has
further subdivided the land use code as follows:

    •   710 – General Office Building
    •   712 – Small Office Building
    •   714 – Corporate Headquarters
    •   715 – Single Tenant Office Building

The setting for all these office land use codes was given as “urban/suburban”. Given the land use code
description provided in PG, Code 710 does not apply as it refers to “a general office building hous[ing]
multiple tenants.” 712 does not apply as it refers to buildings “less than or equal to 5,000 gross square feet in
size.” Land use codes 714 and 715 are quite similar based on the following descriptions and appear equally
applicable to the Scalar project as it will contain offices, meeting rooms, storage space and amenities:

        714 - A corporate headquarters building is a single tenant office building that houses the corporate headquarters of a
        company or organization, which generally consists of offices, meeting rooms, space for file storage and data processing, a
        restaurant or cafeteria, and other service functions.

        715 - A single tenant office building generally contains offices, meeting rooms, and space for file storage and data
        processing of a single business or company and possibly other service functions including a restaurant or cafeteria.

Where 714 and 715 do appear to differ is this:
   1. Average square footage of study sites:
            a. 714: 222,000sf
            b. 715: 96,000sf
   2. Number of studies:
            a. 714: 7
            b. 715: 12
   3. Study area size:
            a. 714: Smallest 65,000sf, with most in excess of 100,000 sf
            b. 715: Half of studies under 75,000sf with 5 studies (42%) in the 25,000sf and 45,000sf range

This comparison seems to suggest that land use code 715 is most applicable to the Scalar project, with the
smallest 42% of its study sites being even more applicable. These study sites have been identified on the 715
scatter plot in Figure 2.
Figure 2. Single Tenant Office Building (Land Use Code 715, GFA)
Average parking generation rates for Code 715 are 3.10 stalls per gross floor area. These demand rates do not
change when only the study sites in the 25,000sf to 45,000sf range are considered. Using these demand rates,
required parking is 61.8 stalls. The site currently provides 72 stalls, which falls within this recommended
range. Therefore, according to the best ITE data available the project as proposed is expected to
meet average parking demand for the long-term future.

Additional factors that could reduce to the project’s parking demand may include the following:
   • Adjacent location of 4 on-street parking stalls on 900 East Street
   • Proximity to Transit
             o Bus route on Pioneer Road
             o ½-mile to TRAX station
   • Location within Draper City Center featuring higher land densities and greater walkability than
        suburban office locations.
   • Availability of bike parking at the project. 12 bike parking stalls are proposed within the structure.

If you have any questions, please contact me at 435.890.4498 or mtaylor@civilsolutionsgroup.net.
Sincerely,




Michael Taylor, P.E.
Civil Solutions Group, Inc.
www.civilsolutionsgroup.net

SCALAR OFFICE EXPANSION
DEVIATION REQUEST
Wednesday, 18 May 2022
Project #: 20077

This project will be removing an existing building that was constructed in 1983 and does not
have any historical value nor does it reflect any of the guidelines of the Town Center Zone. The Owner’s
company is growing and needs to build a larger building to be able to house the company at one location. They
have had the option to purchase/build in other locations within Draper but have not pursued these options as they
appreciate the location they are currently at. The new building will allow the Owner to stay in the heart of Draper
while upgrading the overall appearance of the existing building and site.

The Owner understands the requirements of the Town Center Zone and wants to build a project that both he and
the City of Draper can be proud of. The design requirements of this zone are unique and this project endeavors to
provide a building and site improvements that meet these criteria to extent feasible while meeting the Owners’
goals.



Deviation A – Building Design.

Per 9-22-030 of the Draper City Code, we would like to request the following deviations from the Building Design
Standards and Guidelines:

Parapet

Currently the East façade has a parapet that is longer than 50’ which exceeds 9-22-040(D)(2). The zoning
requirement is to provide parapet variation in long continuous rooflines that exceed 50’-0” The design currently
has modulation in the parapet heights to help break up the profile of the building. We looked at several options to
break up this parapet, but we are restricted on the height of the building per the Town Center Guidelines.
Additionally, this façade does not have the primary entrance and a change in the parapet may draw attention
away from the north façade with the primary entrance.

Articulation

The north and east facades are currently longer than 100’. Based on 9-22-040(C)(2), the design is required to
have significant changes in variation that are at least 5’ in depth for a minimum of 20’ in length. The building was
designed with tight site constraints and embraced the Town Center Zone design language. It uses minor façade
stepping (less than 5’) to help bring in articulation that is more historic in nature. Additionally, the project was
recently reviewed by the Draper Historic Commission who appreciated the attention to detail.

Per 9-22-030 (B) we feel the following deviation criteria apply to the above deviations.

1. The proposed development includes additional amenities or pedestrian and bike connectivity in excess of what
is otherwise required.

          The project serves bicyclists well with a total of 12 indoor and 6 well-lighted outdoor spaces for bike
          parking. Employees that walk or bike can all take advantage of the showers that are in the building.
          With the proximity to public transit and accommodations for bike parking and showering, the project has
          provided more than what is required by the development code.

          Additionally, there is a multi-sport court for the use of Scalar employees that will include a basketball hoop
          and support for pickleball. Adjacent to the multi-sport court there is fixed seating to provide




 Salt Lake City 52 Exchange Place SLC, UT 84111 801.531.1144 | Boise 800 W. Main Street Suite 940 Boise, ID 83702 208.424.7675 | babcockdesign.com
         waiting or resting seats for site patrons. There is also an exterior roof terrace for
         company gatherings, that will have a mix of seating types and outdoor BBQ. These
         amenities are intended for the site patrons (Scalar employees or guests).

         The zoning code does require outdoor seating areas that are convenient to the site
         patrons, for which the multi-sport court and roof terrace accounts for. Additionally, the
         code requires outside bike parking and that has been added to the site. The required
         bike exterior bike parking is provided in addition to the interior secured bike parking.
         This project has met the zoning requirements and has provided additional amenities for the site patrons
         with the addition of the multi-sport court, roof terrace, bike racks, showers, etc.

2. The overall percentage of dedicated public or private landscape and open space area exceeds the required
amount by more than ten percent (10%).

         The landscaping required in the Town Center Zone is 15% of the overall site. The project has 25% and
         meets the above requirements.

6. The variations are consistent with the purpose of this chapter and any applicable master plan or ordinance.

         The building design has really embraced the requirements of the Town Center Zone with the turn of the
         century styling. It has even taken some inspiration from the Granite Power Station with its repeating
         arches. To dress up the building, it has employed the use precast elements to provide a bit more upscale
         look at the arch features and other elements.

9. The amount of primary materials used for a facade is at least ten percent (10%) greater than the minimum
required amount.

    Town Center Zone requires 80% brick minimum (excluding glazing). On the building we have provided an
    average of 91% brick on all facades. This exceeds the amount by the required 10%.


Deviation B Parking Lot Deviations

Parking Count

We are requesting a deviation from the Draper required parking ratio as found in DCMC 9-25-100 Table 9-25-1
for Business as this is a general number meant to work for many different types of businesses. We have
completed a parking study that shows we are withing recommended ranges for the size and type of business.
This study has been completed by an engineer who is licensed in the state of Utah and in compliance with the
provisions of 9-25-090(C). See attached.

Parking Diamonds

Per DCMC 9-25-080(H)(2)(a) there is a requirement for landscaping between the rows of parking unless the
project can demonstrate:
         (1) The site requires a deviation from strict compliance to reduce parking; or
         (2) The site would require a deviation from strict compliance to reduce parking in order to implement
         such landscaping; and
         (3) Constraints of the site would necessitate the elimination of required parking spaces or reduction of
         site boundary landscaping buffers in order to facilitate such landscaping.

The project is requesting to be allowed to utilize tree diamonds between the two rows of parking. As indicated
above, we have commissioned a parking study to reduce the number of parking stalls required for strict
compliance. Additionally, on the East and North property lines there is a public utility easement forcing the
building to sit further West and South. Furthermore, there is a power line on the North side of the building




 Salt Lake City 52 Exchange Place SLC, UT 84111 801.531.1144 | Boise 800 W. Main Street Suite 940 Boise, ID 83702 208.424.7675 | babcockdesign.com
prohibiting the building from being located closer to the street. With the building’s location
due to the easements, powerline, etc., the available area for paring is reduced. And there is
not enough room to provide the required landscaping between the rows of parking. In order
to provide the dividing landscape between rows of parking the project would lose
approximately 16 parking stalls which is well below the parking required by city ordinance or
as outlined as needed in the Parking Study.

We realize the landscaping between the rows helps to screen the parked cars from the view
of the street. One strategy we employed was to have the parking rows perpendicular to the street and provide
oversized landscape islands to provide more opportunity for screening. Finally, it should be noted that as
designed with the tree diamonds, the project complies with the required 10% of the parking lot area landscaped.


Conclusion

This project has been designed to be meet and exceed the Town Center Zone. Additionally, this project was
approved by the Draper Historic Preservation Commission at the March 16, 2022 meeting. The owner is very
interested in building a project that exhibits design excellence with an attention to detail and this design meets
those goals and the Draper Town Center Guidelines. We respectfully request your review of these deviation
requests.
